$comment: Change-impact contract for experts4bit-qlora: which files must (or should) move together. scripts/check_change_impact.py --base <git ref> detects the mechanically detectable triggers from the diff and names the missing companions; the human-readable form is AGENTS.md section 8. Nothing here changes runtime behaviour. File lists are relative to the repository root.
flow: A kernel capability lands and is released in grouped-nf4-gemm first (invariant kernel-first in docs/system-manifest.json).
experts4bit-qlora integrates it behind a version guard or raises the `fast` floor in pyproject.toml to the release that ships it; the pyproject comment ladder records why.

The same change updates docs/system-manifest.json (a new compatibility record, or the current one), docs/capabilities.json (install/environment text), the CI `--requires` assertion and the current solution documents; scripts/check_dependency_floor.py and scripts/check_system_manifest.py hold them equal.

A public entry point that changes (signature, return value, refusal condition) updates its docstring, docs/capabilities.json entrypoints/limitations, the affected docs/solutions page and CHANGELOG.md.

A measured result enters docs/claims.json first, then docs/STATUS.md, then prose that quotes the claim ID; retired and superseded claims are kept, never deleted. README.md is current main: scripts/check_readme_claims.py holds its results table to the register's current values and every position document's ids to the register (CI, discoverability job); scripts/check_claims_register.py holds the register to its own structure -- evidence paths that exist at HEAD, an ISO measured_on on every dated row, successors that resolve, no 'pending' on an active row, a licensed_by verdict row behind every licence label.
The llms bundle is regenerated (python scripts/build_llms_bundle.py) whenever a bundled document changed; --check is a CI gate.
Releases are cut from main by the maintainer; the release note's first paragraph follows docs/RELEASE_NOTES_GUIDE.md.

public-api-change.description: A public entry point changed: a symbol entered or left `__all__`, or a signature, return value or refusal condition of a documented entry point changed.
public-api-change.mechanical_trigger: a symbol added to or removed from `__all__` in experts4bit_qlora/__init__.py
must_consider: the entry point's docstring (when to use, expected layout, what it returns or asserts, refusal conditions, platform needs, the solution page)
docs/capabilities.json (entrypoints, limitations)
docs/solutions/*.md
AGENTS.md section 5
CHANGELOG.md
scripts/wheel_smoke.py (the wheel's promised surface)

new-kernel-capability.description: The consumer side of a capability that landed in grouped-nf4-gemm: this package starts using a kernel, packer, glue or arena primitive the kernel package released.
new-kernel-capability.mechanical_trigger: a kernel import name listed in docs/system-manifest.json packages.kernels.import_names is imported by the package for the first time (warn only; a new use of an already-imported module is not detectable from the diff)
must_consider: pyproject.toml (does the `fast` floor have to rise to the release that ships it? if so, class dependency-floor applies)
docs/system-manifest.json (compatibility record: floor, since, why)
the version guard or capability probe in the engine that uses it (nothing falls back silently)
docs/capabilities.json (entrypoints, environment)
the docs/solutions page that routes to it, and docs/SOLUTIONS.md 'Which of the two packages'
the CI pin of grouped-nf4-gemm and the import tripwire in .github/workflows/ci.yml
a K8 quality arm beside every fused speed arm (docs/METHODOLOGY.md, experts4bit_qlora/k8_gate.py)

measured-result.description: A number or a verdict moved: a claim was added, or an existing claim's status or value changed.
measured-result.mechanical_trigger: docs/claims.json gained a claim id, or a claim's `status` or `value` differs from the base
measured-result.severity: fail (--allow-claims-only: warn, for a register-only correction whose position did not move)
must_consider: the receipt under bench/ (a number is not published before its receipt exists; private receipts are marked evidence_private)

docs/claims.json itself: scripts/check_claims_register.py -- evidence paths exist at HEAD (a receipt is committed before it is named), measured_on is set, a superseded row names its successor, a licence label names its K8 verdict row (licensed_by)
docs/STATUS.md (what you get today / what changed / what is open)
prose that quotes the claim id (README.md, docs/solutions/*.md, docs/SERVING-THROUGHPUT.md, docs/SERVING-PARITY.md)

README.md's results table: scripts/check_readme_claims.py fails when a number there is no longer the named claim's current value, when a row names a superseded or retired id, or when a measured-private claim is presented as measured -- a value or status that moved in the register moves the README row in the same diff
docs/capabilities.json claim_ids (only active statuses may back a capability)
llms-full.txt (regenerate)
never an anchored document: corrections go in a sibling file

dependency-floor.description: The `fast` extra's grouped-nf4-gemm floor moved (or another extra's floor did).
dependency-floor.mechanical_trigger: the grouped-nf4-gemm requirement of `[project.optional-dependencies] fast` in pyproject.toml differs from the base
must_change: docs/system-manifest.json (the compatibility record for this version)
docs/capabilities.json (special_requirements / install text that states the floor)
docs/SOLUTIONS.md and every docs/solutions/*.md that stated the previous floor
must_consider: the pyproject comment ladder (why the floor moved)
README.md install section (it points at the manifest; a number there is drift)
the CI grouped-nf4-gemm pin (a raised floor must not let an older wheel clobber the pinned build)
CHANGELOG.md ('Requires grouped-nf4-gemm >= X for the fast extra')
the sibling repository's copy of docs/system-manifest.json (byte-identical)
